newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov supports realignment of $1 bln light rail.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov supports realignment of $1 bln light rail.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman said Tuesday she supports a plan to relocate portions of a $1.1 billion light rail line from the east side of Hoboken to the west side.

Whitman, speaking at a groundbreaking ceremony for a park redevelopment in Hoboken, said she directed state officials to move the Hudson-Bergen light rail line in response to strong public support for the move.
"The overwhelming sentiment of area residents was in favor of shifting the route," Whitman said.
Residents complained that the original siting for the rail line included too much development along the Hudson River compared to poorer neighborhoods farther away from the waterfront.

Construction on the project began Monday with a groundbreaking ceremony for phase one, a 9.5-mile segment between Bayonne and Hoboken. The realignment move needs approval from federal agencies that are contributing to the financing package.
The New Jersey Transit Corp. is expected to sell $352 million of capital grant anticipation notes on April 29 to help pay for the new rail system.
